content.body:
I was reviewing [the Firefox patch implementing this](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D314004) and it feels super weird to have code like:

```
if (isMove) { UpdateInMicroTask(); } else { UpdateInPostConnectionSteps(); }
```
content.formatted_body:
I was reviewing the Firefox patch implementing this and it feels super weird to have code like:

if (isMove) { UpdateInMicroTask(); } else { UpdateInPostConnectionSteps(); }

content.body: Is it really more async emilio? Seems like if you are in isMove then postConnectionSteps won't be called at all
content.formatted_body: Is it really more async @emilio:mozilla.org? Seems like if you are in isMove then postConnectionSteps won't be called at all

content.body: I guess it would be more obvious if it was in something like updateInPostMoveSteps but I wasn't part of the details here
Noam Rosenthal: right, point being that, on insertion, move steps queue a microtask, but post connection steps do it sync
content.formatted_body: Noam Rosenthal: right, point being that, on insertion, move steps queue a microtask, but post connection steps do it sync

content.body: So yes, it's more async, afaict?
On removal, both queue a microtask, so that's fine
Yea, I thought you meant something else than you did on first read
Yeah our code uses the same code with a flag to implement both post-connection and move steps, so the snippet of code doesn't quite read as the spec, sorry :)
But it made this mismatch much more obvious :)
yeah the rationale is that we have post-insertion steps, but no post-removal and no post-move steps
if we had post-removal or post-move then we would want to use them, but this edge case for doing this stuff with option elements does not justify creating post-removal and post-move steps imo

we could also avoid using post-insertion steps and make that async too, but it ended up making a normal case during parsing become inconsistent about when the options get cloned: https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12263#issuecomment-4743852899
